items.q: That was Muggsy Spanier, Sidney Bechet, Joe Sullivan, Pops Foster, Baby Dodds. The same group that I brought on my Ivy League tour

ctx.x: Who did you bring to Carnegie Hall?

Carnegie Hall. That was Muggsy Spanier, Sidney Bechet, Joe Sullivan, Pops Foster, Baby Dodds. The same group that I brought on my Ivy League tour when we toured the Ivy League schools. You know, showing jazz to the music departments, where I would do a little lecture and illustrate it with music.
Who... Now, when you were approached at Temple to do a concert, why were you approached?

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1989-08-13
items.q: Baby Dodds and Pops Foster were in the band and I knew them well. They had already worked for me a number of times.

ctx.x: And it was a black theater and I used to come out of, out of class and go across the street to the theater all the time, because I knew a lot of the musicians that were, that were playing in the, in the show. And it was during the time when I had first started doing jazz concerts. So it was 1936 and I went backstage, because his band was playing there. And I knew Louis Russell and Red Allen and people that were playing there, Al Nicholas. So, I had, I had met Louis before, I don't actually remember when, but…
Okay, we're on the second reel. Al Rose, same date. August 13th, 1989. Okay, we left off with Eus... Eus Panassia.

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1975-02-03
items.q: both Albert Nicholas and Baby Dodds played in that same pit band... we had, in fact, met before under those conditions.

ctx.x: Oh, well, you mean in the traveling carnivals. Mm-hmm. Of course, I did travel with, uh, with carnivals that belonged to my parents. And, uh, at that time, we did, in fact, have a minstrel show traveling as part of the carnival. And the minstrel show had a pit band that played jazz. Monk Johnson was the leader. Mm-hmm. And, uh, at various times, both Albert Nicholas and Baby Dodds played in that same pit band, and they were both very young. And the only reason I knew that, because I would not have remembered…
What, uh, was the name of the carnival?
